method: Every expectation was written from the sources in src/ by reading them; no analysis tool was run on the sources or on the built inputs, and no tool's detectors or output were looked at. The three inputs are the same program: packed as written, bundled by esbuild, and bundled and minified. Bundling keeps the file names main.js, preload.js, renderer.js and renderer-widget.js and folds the helper modules (config/windows.js, config/endpoints.js, ipc/channels.js, ipc/events.js, ipc/index.js, lib/keys.js, lib/format.js) into the entry files that use them. main.js is written with import statements and is bundled to CommonJS, so in the bundles ipcMain.handle(...) reads import_electron.ipcMain.handle(...) (minified: o.ipcMain.handle(...)) and the two import statements from "electron" become two variables for the same module. Roles and settings are attributed to the four entry files. That is right for the plain input as well, because the helper modules hold constants, option values and formatting functions only: every IPC call, every new BrowserWindow, every exposeInMainWorld, every request and every storage access is written in an entry file. A window setting is attributed to the file that creates the window (main.js), also where the value is written in config/windows.js. After building, the three archives were extracted and the bundled and minified files were read: every call that an expectation rests on is still there, and each expected name is still there as a string in the entry file it is attributed to, with the exceptions that also hold for the sources (timer:tick and the three projects:* names in preload.js are put together from two strings). The commented-out calls exist in the plain input only. An expectation states what the program does, also where that is hard to see; what only looks like a finding is listed under absent. Something that happens only on one platform (dock:badge, tracker.setBadge: macOS) is listed as present, because the code that does it is in the program, and its why says so. webPreferences lists the keys preload, contextIsolation, nodeIntegration and sandbox only and is exhaustive for the values that are fixed in the code: one entry per window and key, so the same key and value appears once for every window that has it. A setting is the value the window is really created with. The invoice window's sandbox is `isDev ? false : true` (minified: `!L`), where isDev is process.env.NODE_ENV === "development": it is decided at run time and therefore is not listed; a tool should show that the key is set from a condition and must not report either value as a fact. The sources also set spellcheck (main window) and backgroundThrottling (widget). describeWindow() in main.js and tracker.runtime in preload.js are objects with the keys sandbox, contextIsolation and nodeIntegration whose values are read from the running process; they are reports, not settings. Requests: shell.openExternal(address) hands an address to the operating system, which opens it in the user's browser; the application itself requests nothing, so such addresses are absent and the call is not a request call (it is not counted in unreadable either).

renderer.js loadEntries: fetch with a template: the constant API_BASE from config/endpoints.js (it ends in a slash), the fixed part projects/, then a run-time project id (and /entries?week= with a run-time week)
renderer.js exchangeRate: fetch with a concatenation in which the constant is the host: "https://" + RATES_HOST + "/latest?base=" + a run-time currency

renderer.js loadClients: fetch(new URL("clients", API_BASE)); a relative path resolved against a base that ends in a slash (checked with node: new URL("clients", "https://api.punchclock.example/v3/").href)

renderer.js loadTimesheet: a URL object is made with new URL("timesheets/current", API_BASE), gets a query parameter tz with a run-time value (url.searchParams.set), and is then given to fetch. The request goes to .../timesheets/current?tz=<time zone>; the part before the query is fixed
renderer.js saveEntry: a Request object is built with new Request(literal, { method: "POST", ... }) and given to fetch
renderer.js deleteEntry: fetch(API_BASE + "entries/" + entryId, { method: "DELETE" })
renderer.js savePreferences: window.fetch with a literal and { method: "PATCH" }
renderer.js uploadInvoice: XMLHttpRequest.open("POST", links.upload); the address is the property upload of the object links in config/endpoints.js
renderer.js openTeamFeed: new WebSocket(`${links.live}/team/${teamId}`); links.live is defined in config/endpoints.js
renderer-widget.js serviceStatus: fetch(STATUS_URL, { cache: "no-store" }); the constant is defined in config/endpoints.js

endpoints.unreadableWhy: renderer.js downloadReceipt calls fetch(receipt.downloadUrl); the address is a run-time value of which nothing is known at the call. A tool should show the call and say the URL is unknown. Every other request call has an address that is known at least in its leading part. shell.openExternal(url) in the window-open handler of main.js also has a run-time argument, but it is not a request call (see method) and is not counted
